note:
Scale-to-zero coverage, stated precisely.

Configured: all three endpoints now run a 0.5 CU floor, the minimum Lakebase allows. Two of three (dev-work-order-notes and forecast-deferred-maintenance) also carry a 300s idle suspend, so an idle branch costs close to nothing.

Not configured: the production endpoint still carries the 86400s suspend it was created with. This is a limitation we hit, not a design choice. Every update_mask path tried for that field was rejected with 'Unknown field path in update_mask': suspend_timeout_duration, spec.suspend_timeout_duration, spec.settings.suspend_timeout_duration and settings.suspend_timeout_duration. Setting spec.default_endpoint_settings on the PROJECT succeeds, but applies to endpoints created afterwards, which is why the forecasting branch (created after that change) picked up 300s and the two pre-existing endpoints did not. Deleting and recreating the production endpoint would inherit the new default, but the Lakebase CDF config and the dim_tag_online synced table both depend on that endpoint, so it was left alone deliberately rather than risk the submission evidence.

We have no evidence that a root branch is excluded from scale-to-zero by design. The 86400s value is simply what the project was created with before the default was changed.
